title: Effectiveness of Resonance Frequency Breathing Exercises in Patients With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Central Sensitization
off: Effectiveness of Resonance Frequency Breathing Exercises in Patients With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Central Sensitization
summary:
Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by systemic inflammation, fatigue, central sensitization, and chronic pain. While physical exercise is strongly recommended to enhance functional capacity and manage fatigue, heightened central sensitivity and pain often limit adherence and clinical gains.

Resonance frequency breathing (paced diaphragmatic breathing at 6 breaths per minute, 0.1 Hz) stimulates the baroreflex and facilitates autonomic regulation, which may alleviate central pain processing. This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of resonance frequency breathing added to a standard exercise program compared with exercise alone on central sensitization, pain thresholds, fatigue, pain catastrophizing, functional capacity, respiratory muscle strength, disease activity, and quality of life in patients with SLE.

Participants will be randomly allocated to either a Standard Exercise Group or a Standard Exercise + Resonance Breathing Group for an 8-week intervention.
desc:
This is a prospective, two-arm, parallel-group, single-blind randomized controlled clinical trial. Eligible patients diagnosed with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus will be randomized into two arms:

Control Group: Receives an 8-week multi-component standard exercise program (aerobic, resistance, range of motion, and stretching exercises).

Intervention Group: Receives the identical 8-week standard exercise program combined with slow resonance frequency breathing training at 6 breaths per minute (0.1 Hz) guided by the offline mobile application "Prana Breath".

Clinical and functional assessments will be conducted at baseline (Week 0) and at the end of the intervention (Week 8).
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Clinically diagnosed with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) according to the 2019 ACR/EULAR classification criteria
* Aged between 18 and 65 years
* Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) score of 40 or higher (CSI \>= 40)
* Stable medical therapy with no pharmacological regimen changes within the last 3 months
* Willing and cognitively able to provide written informed consent and adhere to the intervention protocol

Exclusion Criteria:

* Presence of severe cardiovascular or pulmonary contraindications that preclude safe participation in exercise or paced breathing training
* Major surgical operation within the preceding 6 months
* Current pregnancy
* Active severe disease flare-up
* Regular and ongoing practice of structured breathing exercises, pranayama, or yoga

arms.d: Participants receive an 8-week multi-component standard exercise program including aerobic exercise, progressive resistance training, range of motion, and stretching exercises. Supervised clinical sessions are conducted twice weekly, complemented by home exercises to achieve 150 minutes of weekly aerobic activity.

Participants receive the identical 8-week standard exercise program combined with diaphragmatic resonance frequency breathing at 6 breaths per minute (0.1 Hz) with a 4:6 inhalation-to-exhalation ratio using a pursed-lip technique. Breathing practice is performed daily (10-20 min/day), guided by the offline mobile application "Prana Breath" and a printed instructional brochure.

primary.m: Change in Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) Score

x.titre: Respiration à fréquence de résonance associée à l'exercice dans le lupus avec sensibilisation centrale
x.question: Ajouter une respiration lente à 6 cycles par minute à un programme d'exercice réduit-il la sensibilisation centrale chez des patients lupiques ?
x.contexte:
Le lupus s'accompagne souvent de fatigue, de douleur chronique et de sensibilisation centrale. L'exercice physique est fortement recommandé pour améliorer la capacité fonctionnelle et la fatigue, mais l'hypersensibilité à la douleur limite l'adhésion et les gains cliniques.

La respiration à fréquence de résonance (respiration diaphragmatique à 6 cycles par minute, soit 0,1 Hz) stimule le baroréflexe et favorise la régulation autonome, ce qui pourrait atténuer le traitement central de la douleur. Cette approche a été étudiée dans d'autres douleurs chroniques.

Cet essai randomisé en simple aveugle, mené à l'université d'Istanbul-Cerrahpaşa, inclut environ 38 patients lupiques avec un score de sensibilisation centrale (CSI) ≥ 40. Les deux groupes suivent 8 semaines d'exercice standard (aérobie, renforcement, amplitudes, étirements). Le groupe intervention y ajoute la respiration guidée par l'application Prana Breath, avec un rapport inspiration/expiration de 4:6.
x.interet: Elle pourrait valider une intervention peu coûteuse pour améliorer la douleur centrale et l'adhésion à l'exercice dans le lupus. L'effectif réduit et la durée de 8 semaines limitent la portée.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 65 ans atteints de lupus avec sensibilisation centrale (CSI ≥ 40).
inclusion: Consentement écrit et capacité à suivre le protocole
exclusion: Contre-indication cardiovasculaire ou pulmonaire à l'exercice ou à la respiration contrôlée
Pratique régulière d'exercices respiratoires, de pranayama ou de yoga

bras.traitement: Programme de 8 semaines : aérobie, renforcement progressif, amplitudes articulaires, étirements
Même programme plus respiration diaphragmatique à 6 cycles/min (rapport 4:6) avec l'application Prana Breath

x.critere: Variation du score CSI entre l'inclusion et la semaine 8
